source.title: Dynamics-Aware Loss for Learning with Label Noise
source.authors: Xiu-Chuan Li; Xiao-Bo Xia; Fei Zhu; Tong-Liang Liu; Xu-Yao Zhang; Cheng-Lin Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures training-accuracy trajectories on correctly and wrongly labeled examples, bearing on whether networks learn the shared real-label patterns before fitting noisy labels.
record.gate_note: The claim that DNNs fit any ratio of noisy labels appears in the Introduction as a result from cited work [1], not this study's own result. Figure 4 and its accompanying text report this study's training-accuracy trajectories for CIFAR-100 with 40% instance-dependent noise.
record.test_reason: Section 5.4 and Figure 4 report the study's own clean-label and wrong-label training trajectories, directly bearing on V6. The study also uses this learning sequence to design DAL.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report learning dynamics consistent with early clean-pattern learning and later noise fitting, and conclude that DAL exploits these dynamics to retain rapid early learning while suppressing later noise fitting and improving generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains ResNet18 on partially corrupted CIFAR-100 using CE, GCE, and DAL, and examines label-stratified training-accuracy trajectories; it does not reproduce the original random-labeling experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trajectories differ by loss: CE reaches 100% accuracy on wrong labels, GCE's wrong-label accuracy rises late, and DAL keeps it low.
record.problems: The claim-relevant training-accuracy trajectories are shown in Figure 4 without exact values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The study reports one corruption condition for this analysis: CIFAR-100 with 40% instance-dependent noise.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version rows extracted. Table 2–5 report test accuracy for loss-function comparisons or combined methods, but do not test the training behaviors specified by V1–V6.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero whole-training-set error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios for true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption fractions together with a test-error trajectory from clean labels to fully random labels. Benchmark test accuracies alone do not establish this joint behavior.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.

Completely random labeling and generality across architectures, datasets, and corruption rates; the label-stratified trajectory analysis uses one CIFAR-100 condition with 40% instance-dependent noise.

missing.what: MAE yields training accuracy below 10% on both correctly and wrongly labeled examples. Add the two subset results as an underfitting control; the stated endpoints alone cannot establish V6's temporal ordering.

The general early-clean versus delayed-wrong trajectory description is not captured in R3's GCE clean-label endpoint summary. Record the applicable clean-label trajectory from Figure 4 to substantiate the GCE timing comparison.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any version. Its introductory assertion about fitting arbitrary noise ratios is cited prior work. Figure 4's numerical curves are not recoverable precisely from the supplied text; the verdicts rely on the accompanying explicit descriptions.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error with test error at chance, without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training-time cost relative to true labels and convergence as corrupted-label fraction increases.
Fitting shuffled, permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Whether training error stays perfect across corruption fractions and test error rises steadily toward chance.
Whether the listed regularizers stop random-label fitting or their removal affects true-label generalization.

The study tests one CIFAR-100 condition with 40% instance-dependent noise, not completely random labels or multiple corruption fractions; its DAL result does not show later memorization of noisy labels.

rows.operation_detail: Train with cross-entropy on CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent label noise; track training accuracy by label correctness over epochs.
rows.value: The training accuracy on correctly labeled data increases fast at the outset.
rows.note: The text describes the trajectory; Figure 4 provides no tabulated values.
rows.check: The early clean-label rise is correctly recorded. The text additionally states that CE eventually reaches 100% accuracy on correctly labeled examples.

rows.subject: ResNet18 trained with CE
rows.operation_detail: Train with cross-entropy on CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent label noise; track training accuracy by label correctness over epochs.
rows.value: The training accuracy on wrongly labeled data rises slowly initially and grows quickly after several epochs; it reaches 100% on wrongly labeled data.
rows.note: The 100% statement refers to CE in the accompanying discussion; the trajectory is described qualitatively.

rows.subject: ResNet18 trained with GCE
rows.operation_detail: Train with generalized cross-entropy on CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent label noise; track training accuracy by label correctness over epochs.
rows.value: The model can achieve high training accuracy on correctly labeled data finally.
rows.note: No exact trajectory values are stated.
rows.check: High final clean-label accuracy alone does not establish when those labels were learned relative to noisy labels. Interpret alongside R4 and the general trajectory description in Section 5.4.

rows.subject: ResNet18 trained with GCE
rows.operation_detail: Train with generalized cross-entropy on CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent label noise; track training accuracy by label correctness over epochs.
rows.value: Training accuracy on wrongly labeled data is relatively low compared with CE, but still rises remarkably at the late stage.
rows.note: The late rise is explicitly described; no exact values are stated.
rows.check: The late rise is explicitly reported. The comparison with CE is consistent with the surrounding discussion, although the source's parenthetical comparisons in this sentence appear inconsistent.

source_check.correct: GCE wrong-label training accuracy rises markedly late in training. The source describes its level as relatively low compared with MAE, an internally inconsistent comparison given the reported MAE accuracy below 10%. Comparison with CE is a plausible repair, but is not the comparison explicitly stated.
source_check.problem: The recorded comparison with CE silently repairs the source's inconsistent comparison with MAE.

rows.subject: ResNet18 trained with DAL
rows.operation_detail: Train with dynamics-aware loss on CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent label noise; track training accuracy by label correctness over epochs.
rows.value: Training accuracy on correctly labeled data rises rapidly.
rows.note: No exact trajectory values are stated.
rows.check: Correctly records the early clean-label learning component; this row alone does not establish subsequent noise memorization.

rows.subject: ResNet18 trained with DAL
rows.operation_detail: Train with dynamics-aware loss on CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent label noise; track training accuracy by label correctness over epochs.
rows.value: Training accuracy on wrongly labeled data remains at a low level.
rows.note: This condition does not show later memorization of noisy labels.
rows.check: DAL preserves early clean-label learning but suppresses subsequent wrong-label fitting. This is a deliberately modified loss condition.
